summary: preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes 727KB obfuscated sibling payload on installer host
details: The package declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. Both setup.mjs and its sibling math_init.js are heavily obfuscated. setup.mjs uses obfuscator.io-style transforms (rotating `_0x` identifiers, per-call wrapper-object indirection such as `_0x19328d.YCZJE(execFileSync,...)`, and string aliasing) that hide the arguments to `execFileSync` and the control flow. At install time it looks for `bun` on PATH, otherwise downloads a platform-specific Bun 1.3.13 archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts and chmod+x's the binary, and invokes it against `math_init.js` — a 727KB single-line module beginning with `// @bun @bun-cjs` and containing a rotated string-array (`WV8StW` shift routine) plus a character-map decoder. The actual behavior of the code that runs on the installer host cannot be determined without executing the obfuscated Bun-only bytecode-style payload. Fetching Bun from its official release host is not itself the issue; the issue is that opaque, obfuscated code with no source form is auto-executed on every `npm install` under a freshly-fetched alternate runtime that bypasses Node-scoped tooling and review.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
